units: C (preferred temperature range, PTR, of selected body temperature Tsel; sexes pooled)
method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice: body temperature of lizards in a laboratory glass terrarium gradient, 20 to 60 C
conditions: Introduced population at Es Canutells, southern Menorca (Balearic Islands, Spain). 24 wild adult lizards (14 males, 10 females) noosed during their daily activity period and taken to the laboratory in Es Castell, where they were housed in individual terraria on mealworms and crickets with water ad libitum; no acclimation period is reported in the text read. Gradient in a glass terrarium (100 x 60 x 60 cm) with a 150 W infrared lamp over one side, 20 to 60 C; Tsel was measured between 12 and 14 June 2013 (late spring by the paper's own season definition), one reading per lizard each hour from 08:00 to 17:00 h (GMT) with a digital thermometer. The Discussion prints the same 50% range as 28.40 to 31.70 C ('obtained in the late spring'), against 28.40 to 31.57 C in the Abstract and Results; the record follows the two agreeing printings. The Methods define the PTR as the central 50% of Tsel values and also report an 80% PTR of 26.85 to 32.54 C (Results, not in the quote); the Results give mean Tsel of males 29.84 +/- 0.41 C (SE; n = 14) and females 30.15 +/- 0.31 C (SE; n = 10), one-way ANOVA F1,22 = 0.301, P = 0.589, and the sexes were pooled for the range. Lizards were released at their capture places after the experiment. Gradient choice, not a receptor threshold.
